extracted.intended_audience: hearing examiners, agency counsel, administrative law practitioners, agency adjudication staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and measurement conventions for appeals from intermediate (initial/recommended/tentative) hearing examiner decisions, and related time-computation and workload metrics for examiners across federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Appeal - Filing Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: (PRESIDENT'S CONFERENCE ILLUSTRATIVE RULE (a)) "Any party may appeal ... by filing a notice of appeal with the agency within ten days after service upon him of such decision."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix table shows agencies set various filing periods (common values in the table: 10, 15, 20, 30 days). The PCAP suggested rule uses 10 days; practitioners should check the specific agency rule listed in the appendix (e.g., 10 CFR 2.751-.752; 14 CFR 301.26; 47 CFR 1.153 etc.) because times vary by agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions - Filing Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: (PRESIDENT'S CONFERENCE ILLUSTRATIVE RULE (b)) "An appeal may be perfected by filing exceptions to such intermediate decision within twenty days after service of the decision."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix agency matrix indicates agencies differ on the period allowed to file exceptions (some permit 15, 20, or 30 days). Always confirm the agency-specific deadline rather than assuming the illustrative 20-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Exceptions / Stay of Intermediate Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: (PRESIDENT'S CONFERENCE ILLUSTRATIVE RULE (c)) "The effectiveness of the intermediate decision shall be stayed if any party files a notice of appeal and exceptions within the times specified above or if the agency upon notice to the parties undertakes to review the decision. Otherwise, the intermediate decision shall become the final decision of the agency."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some agencies explicitly authorize the hearing examiner or agency official to stay the intermediate decision (example: Coast Guard rules, 46 CFR 137.11-15). The appendix includes a column indicating whether taking an appeal stays the intermediate order; practice varies, so check the agency's rule for whether automatic stay occurs or whether a stay is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies to Exceptions - Filing Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: (PRESIDENT'S CONFERENCE ILLUSTRATIVE RULE (d)) "Within ten days after service of exceptions, any opposing party may file a reply to such exceptions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may set different reply periods; the illustrative rule uses 10 days. The appendix shows which agencies provide a reply period and what length; confirm agency rule and whether the agency permits enlargement of reply time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and Form of Exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: (PRESIDENT'S CONFERENCE ILLUSTRATIVE RULE (e)) "Exceptions shall identify specifically the findings, conclusions, or proposed action to which objection is made, and shall be supported by concise argument and by specific page references to the parts of the record and the legal and other authorities relied upon."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions must be specific and supported: identify the precise findings or conclusions being challenged, provide concise argumentation, and cite record pages and legal authorities. The appendix also denotes which agencies prescribe a particular form of exceptions; follow any agency-prescribed form and citation requirements exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlargement of Time
rubrics_metrics.description: (PRESIDENT'S CONFERENCE ILLUSTRATIVE RULE (f)) "The time periods prescribed by this rule may be extended by the agency for good cause."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most agency rules permit enlargement for good cause; the agency matrix includes a column 'Agency may enlarge time.' Where allowed, parties should file timely motions or stipulations per the agency rule. Some agencies set explicit limits on extensions (see agency-specific citations in the appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Time — Exclude Initial Day
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix provision (1): "Exclude initial day of period."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When computing filing periods, do not count the day of the triggering event (e.g., date of service) unless an agency rule specifies otherwise. This is one of several computation conventions tabulated in the appendix; verify the particular agency's rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Time — Include Last Day
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix provision (2): "Include last day of period."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the cited agency conventions, the final day of the prescribed period is counted as a filing day. If the final day falls on a weekend/holiday, other rules may apply (see next entry). Confirm the agency-specific computation rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Time — Weekend/Holiday Rule for Last Day
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix provision (3): "When last day of period falls on a Saturday, Sunday or holiday the period is extended to include the next business day."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many agencies extend filing deadlines to the next business day when the deadline lands on a non-business day; some agencies have different definitions of 'legal holiday' or business hours—check the specific agency regulation (examples and citations are provided in the appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Time — Short-period Weekend/Holiday Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix provision (4): "When period is less than seven days, intermediate Saturdays, Sundays and holidays are excluded."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For short filing periods (under seven days), intermediate weekends and holidays often are not counted. Agencies differ: some include intermediate Saturdays in certain cases; consult the agency rule for precise treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Time — Including Intermediate Sundays/Holidays
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix provision (5): "Specific provision for including intermediate Sundays and holidays."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minority of agency rules explicitly include intermediate Sundays/holidays in the computation; the appendix indicates which agencies adopt this convention. Always check the agency-specific provision rather than assuming exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of Time — Part-holiday, Business-day, and Filing-hour Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix notes: "Part holiday not considered a holiday." and agency-specific notes such as 'Saturday is considered a business day', 'Legal holiday means Federal legal holiday', and 'Any document lodged with the Commission after 5 p.m. shall be deemed ... next succeeding business day.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency rules vary on treatment of half-holidays, local vs. federal holidays, business-day definitions, and cut-off hours for filings. The appendix cross-references many specific agency regulations (e.g., 39 CFR, 31 CFR, etc.) providing examples; follow the precise agency rule for these temporal definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic Extension for Mail or Location-based Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory comment: "Automatic extension of time based on location of parties or method of service of documents."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seven agencies have automatic extension provisions. Typically three agencies add three days when service is by mail; a fourth agency adds three days only when the time allowed following service by mail is ten days or less. Check whether an agency adds days for mail service or for parties in designated geographical areas, and whether that rule applies to the particular filing at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Time Under Advisement (measurement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 11 footnote: "For purposes of this table the period of time under advisement by an examiner is measured from final submission to the examiner, that is, the date the last brief and proposed findings were filed, to issuance of the examiner's decision."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When agencies report or compute 'time under advisement' use this measurement convention; note that historical reports combined certain shorter intervals differently (e.g., 1957 columns combined), so comparative statistics may reflect different binning conventions across years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Total Time from Assignment to Examiner to Decision (measurement and agency variation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 10 notes and footnotes explain that 'total time from assignment to examiner to decision by examiner' is the reporting metric, but agencies may measure from different starting points (e.g., from opening of hearing or from prehearing conference, or the date examiner was directed to hold a hearing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that agencies differ in what they count as the start date (CAB uses opening of the hearing or prehearing conference; FMB in 1957 computed from the date examiner was directed to hold a hearing). Such measurement differences affect cross-agency and year-to-year comparisons; review footnotes for agency-specific measurement conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition & Computation — Examiner Man-Years and Decisions per Man-Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 12 footnotes: examiner man-years 'includes the time of chief examiners, and takes into account entrances upon and separations from service as well as inter-agency loans of examiners, without reduction for any time necessarily spent in training new personnel or in other duties "not inconsistent with duties and responsibilities as examiners." The column for average decisions per man-year 'relates only to decisions on the merits in contested cases in those types of proceedings which are the subject of the foregoing tables.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using examiner workload metrics, include chief examiner time, account for personnel changes and loans, and exclude time reductions for unrelated duties only if the agency rule so directs. Note additional adjustments noted in footnotes: excluding non-hearing safety enforcement proceedings or consent/default decisions can materially change the average decisions-per-man-year figure; consult footnotes for agency-specific exclusions/adjustments.
